anomalies.observed: The 3.3 V rail is split into two nets that are never joined. The LDO output and every sensor/peripheral are on net "+3.3V" (REG2 pin 1 "OUT" is on +3.3V), while the MCU side (all FCC/NAVC decoupling caps C16-C26/C40-C48, I2C pull-ups, SWD and expansion connectors) sits on a separate net "+3V3" that has no source and no tie to +3.3V. In addition the MCU supply pins themselves are on no rail at all: FCC1 pins 11/27/50/75/100 (VDD), pin 6 (VBAT) and pin 21 (VDDA) and NAVC1 pins 19/32/48/64 (VDD) appear only on nets named "unconnected-(...)".
anomalies.expected: A single 3V3 rail sourced by the LD39200PU33R LDO should power both MCUs and all I2C sensor ICs, per the spec: "3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs".
anomalies.impact: Neither MCU receives 3.3 V: their VDD/VBAT/VDDA pins are floating and the "+3V3" net driven by the LDO is a different net than the one the MCU-side circuitry sits on. The board would not power up or run.

anomalies.observed: The UART3 debug connector's data pins are wired to FCC1 pins 48 and 73, which the symbol defines as VCAP (the 1.2 V core-regulator output pins), not to USART3 pins: net "UART3_TX_FCC" = {FCC1.48 (VCAP), UART3_FCC1.3} and net "UART3_RX_FCC" = {FCC1.73 (VCAP), UART3_FCC1.4}. The FCC's actual UART-capable pins used elsewhere (PD8/PD9) are left unused (FCC1.55 unconnected, FCC1.56 on GPIO_A_FCC). The intended VCAP decoupling capacitor C13 (2u2) is left floating as "unconnected-(C13-Pad1)".
anomalies.expected: VCAP pins must each have a 2.2 uF capacitor to GND (datasheet requirement) and must not be routed to an external connector; a UART3 header should be wired to the MCU's USART3 TX/RX pins.
anomalies.impact: The core-voltage pins lose their required decoupling and are exposed on an external header; the MCU core regulator can oscillate/brown out and the UART3 port is non-functional (and a connected cable would load the core rail).

anomalies.observed: The FCC HSE crystal is wired to FCC1 pin 5 (PE6) and pin 37 (PE7) rather than the oscillator pins PH0/PH1 (pins 12/13); PH0 instead carries C14 (2u2) and PH1 carries the VDDA/VREF filter (C30, R21). On the NAVC, the HSE crystal net (HSE_IN_NAVC / HSE_OUT_NAVC) contains no MCU pin at all, while the 2.2 uF core caps C37/C38 are placed on NAVC1 pin 5 (PH0) and pin 6 (PH1), and NAVC1's VCAP pins 31/47 are unconnected.
anomalies.expected: The 25 MHz HSE crystal must be connected to the MCU OSC_IN/OSC_OUT pins (PH0/PH1 on both the STM32H753 and STM32F405), and the 2.2 uF VCAP capacitors must sit on the VCAP pins, not on the oscillator pins.

evidence.quote: HSE crystal (both MCUs) | FCC / NAVC | ABM8G-25.000MHZ-4Y-T3

anomalies.impact: The crystals are not connected to the oscillator pins of either MCU (and the NAVC crystal is not connected to the MCU at all), while the core decoupling sits on the oscillator pins; neither MCU can start its HSE clock, so the board cannot boot at the specified 25 MHz.

parsed.summary: The files show the Hades 3.3 V rail and both MCUs' supply/clock pins disconnected from the intended design (LDO output on a separate "+3.3V" net, MCU VDD/VBAT/VDDA floating, crystals not on the OSC pins), and the FCC UART3 header is bridged onto the core VCAP pins, so the board as built would not power up or clock and would mis-route its debug UART.
